Measured 2026-09-13 in evo-flight-lab:sealed, linux/arm64, network none.
Source: visibility-pragma-oracle.c. Compilers: gcc-14 and clang-19.
No full build copies or probe binaries retained.

Declaration cases (N=1..9):
  $CC -std=gnu11 -fpie -O2 -DCASE=$N -c probe.c -o /tmp/probe.o
  readelf -Ws /tmp/probe.o

CASE  GCC exit / data visibility          Clang exit / data visibility
1     0 HIDDEN                            0 HIDDEN
2     0 HIDDEN                            0 HIDDEN
3     0 DEFAULT                           0 DEFAULT
4     0 HIDDEN (conflicting warning)      1 (visibility does not match)
5     0 DEFAULT                           0 DEFAULT
6     0 DEFAULT (unmatched-pop warning)   1 (no matching push)
7     0 PROTECTED                         0 PROTECTED
8     0 HIDDEN                            0 HIDDEN
9     0 HIDDEN                            0 HIDDEN

Profile: hidden/default only, as for the existing visibility attribute.
Cases 4 and 6 refuse E2943 in the conflicting oracles' refusal direction.
Case 7 is not admitted by the authorized visibility vocabulary.

Address cases (no CASE, HIDDEN=0/1):
  $CC -std=gnu11 -O2 $MODE -DHIDDEN=$HIDDEN -S probe.c -o /tmp/probe.s
Both compilers return 0 for every row; inspect address_data/address_weak:
MODE       HIDDEN   strong data    weak data
-fno-pie   0        direct         GOT
-fno-pie   1        direct         GOT
-fpie      0        GOT            GOT
-fpie      1        direct         GOT
-fPIC      0        GOT            GOT
-fPIC      1        direct         GOT

Direct = adrp + page-offset, not a load through :got: / :got_lo12:.
Weak addresses still use the GOT even when hidden: unresolved weak is null.
